speaker: Doctor
text: Has the infant passed any stool, even a small amount, since birth? I would like to examine the abdomen for any palpable masses or tenderness.

text: I will now examine the infant's abdomen for distension and tenderness. I am also going to perform a digital rectal examination to assess for stool retention or a narrow anal canal.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Newborn, no prior medical history. Birth was uneventful. Social history: The infant is the first child of the family. No known family history of genetic or congenital diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will now perform a digital rectal examination to check for a narrow anal canal or stool retention, which is critical for distinguishing between Hirschsprung disease and meconium ileus. Following the exam, I need to know if there is a family history of Cystic Fibrosis, as meconium ileus is strongly associated with it.

speaker: Patient
text: The infant shows signs of distress, possibly due to abdominal discomfort.

speaker: Doctor
text: The infant's distress and clinical picture strongly suggest a lower intestinal obstruction, likely meconium ileus or Hirschsprung disease. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of dilated bowel loops with no gas in the rectum confirm a distal obstruction, strongly pointing towards meconium ileus or Hirschsprung disease. To distinguish between these, I need to evaluate for a transition zone or perform a contrast enema. REQUEST TEST: Contrast Enema

speaker: Doctor
text: A normal contrast enema result is unusual for typical meconium ileus or Hirschsprung disease, so I need to rule out other causes like meconium plug syndrome or small left colon syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Sweat Chloride Test

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal sweat chloride test effectively rules out Cystic Fibrosis and makes meconium ileus highly unlikely. Given the distal obstruction on X-ray but a normal contrast enema, I suspect a functional obstruction like meconium plug syndrome or perhaps a missed transition zone in Hirschsprung's. I will request histological confirmation to be certain. REQUEST TEST: Rectal Suction Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Histopathology shows absence of ganglion cells in the submucosa and myenteric plexus, consistent with Hirschsprung’s disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: The histopathology results showing an absence of ganglion cells confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's disease
